newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech crown falls ahead of cen bank meeting.
newsitem.headline: Czech crown falls ahead of cen bank meeting.

text.p: The Czech crown fell against its mark/dollar basket on Thursday morning ahead of the central bank's regular Thursday afternoon board meeting where dealers believe a relaxation of monetary policy will be considered.

The crown had dropped around 50 basis points against the basket mid-point in the first hour of trading to 26.609 against the dollar and 17.229 versus the mark implying a deviation from the mid-point of 1.32 percent.

"There are two factors (explaining the fall): the central bank meeting today, the other is expectation about what the central bank and the government will do to stimulate the economy next Wednesday," said Breta Tichanek of ING Bank.

The Czech economy has run into serious problems in recent months with the latest batch of bad news coming on Wednesday morning when official figures showed industrial production falling 5.8 percent year-on-year in February.

The government is due to announce a package of measures to reinvigorate the economy next Wednesday. However, many analysts say it will be difficult to kick start the economy without a relaxation of monetary policy.
In the middle of last year, the Czech central bank raised the discount rate by one percentage point to 10.5 percent and minimum reserve requirements were increased to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent.
Real interest rates have been moving even higher as inflation has fallen sharply. March inflation dropped to 6.8 percent year-on-year from 7.3 percent in February.
